questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
The acceleration-time relationship for a vehicle subjected to non-uniform acceleration is,

\[\frac{dv}{dt} = (\alpha - \beta v_0)e^{-\beta t} \]

where, \(v\) is the speed in m/s, \(t\) is the time in s, \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are parameters, and \(v_0\) is the initial speed in m/s. If the accelerating behavior of a vehicle, whose driver intends to overtake a slow moving vehicle ahead, is described as,

\[\frac{dv}{dt} = (\alpha - \beta v) \]

Considering \(\alpha = 2 \text{ m/s}^2\), \(\beta = 0.05 \text{ s}^{-1}\) and \(\frac{dv}{dt} = 1.3 \text{ m/s}^2\) at \(t = 3\) s, the distance (in m) travelled by the vehicle in 35 s is __________.
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Traffic Engineering (Vehicle Kinematics)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Acceleration: \(a(t) = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = (\alpha - \beta v_0)e^{-\beta t}\)
    • Parameters: \(\alpha = 2\text{ m/s}^2\), \(\beta = 0.05\text{ s}^{-1}\)
    • Condition: at \(t = 3\text{ s}\), \(a = 1.3\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the distance travelled (\(S\)) in 35 seconds.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Velocity is the integral of acceleration: \(v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt + v_0\)
  • Distance is the integral of velocity: \(S(t) = \int v(t)\,dt\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Find initial velocity (\(v_0\)) from the condition at \(t = 3\text{ s}\).
  2. Integrate \(a(t)\) to derive velocity function \(v(t)\).
  3. Integrate \(v(t)\) from \(0\) to \(35\text{ s}\) to find total distance.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find \(v_0\):
    \[(2 - 0.05v_0)e^{-0.05 \times 3} = 1.3 \]\[2 - 0.05v_0 = 1.3 \times e^{0.15} \approx 1.3 \times 1.16183 = 1.51038 \]\[v_0 = \frac{2 - 1.51038}{0.05} = 9.7924\text{ m/s} \]
  2. Formulate Velocity Function \(v(t)\):
    \[v(t) = \int(\alpha - \beta v_0)e^{-\beta t}\,dt = \frac{\alpha}{\beta} - \left(\frac{\alpha}{\beta} - v_0\right)e^{-\beta t} \]
    With \(\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta} = \dfrac{2}{0.05} = 40\):
    \[v(t) = 40 - (40 - 9.7924)e^{-0.05t} = 40 - 30.2076\,e^{-0.05t} \]
  3. Calculate Distance in 35 s:
    \[S(35) = \int_0^{35}\left(40 - 30.2076\,e^{-0.05t}\right)dt \]\[ S(35) = \left[40t + \frac{30.2076}{0.05}e^{-0.05t}\right]_0^{35} = \left[40t + 604.152\,e^{-0.05t}\right]_0^{35} \]\[S(35) = (1400 + 604.152 \times 0.17377) - (0 + 604.152) \]\[S(35) = 1400 + 104.985 - 604.152 = 900.83\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 900.83 m  |  Accepted key range: 895 to 905

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q62
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: On a circular curve, the rate of superelevation is \(e\). While negotiating the curve a vehicle comes to a stop. It is seen that the stopped vehicle does not slide inwards (in the radial direction). The coefficient of side friction is \(f\). Which of the following is true:
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Geometric Design (Horizontal Curves)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Superelevation rate: \(e\)
    • Stopped vehicle (\(v = 0\)) does not slide inwards
    • Coefficient of lateral friction: \(f\)
  • Aim: Identify the correct relationship between \(e\) and \(f\).

3. Core Concepts:

When a vehicle halts on a superelevated curve (banked at angle \(\theta\)), the centrifugal force is zero. Forces parallel to the road surface are:

  • Gravity component pulling inwards: \(W\sin\theta\)
  • Resisting friction acting outwards: \(fN = fW\cos\theta\)

For the vehicle not to slide inwards: Inward Force \(\leq\) Outward Friction Capacity.

4. Solution Method:

Set up the no-sliding inequality:

\[W\sin\theta \leq fW\cos\theta \implies \tan\theta \leq f \]

Since rate of superelevation \(e = \tan\theta\):

\[e \leq f \]

5. Final Answer:

Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q63
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: A sign is required to be put up asking drivers to slow down to 30 km/h before entering Zone Y (see figure). On this road, vehicles require 174 m to slow down to 30 km/h (the distance of 174 m includes the distance travelled during the perception-reaction time of drivers). The sign can be read by 6/6 vision drivers from a distance of 48 m. The sign is placed at a distance of x m from the start of Zone Y so that even a 6/9 vision driver can slow down to 30 km/h before entering the zone. The minimum value of x is __________ m.
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Geometric Design (Sight Distance)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Distance to slow down to \(30\text{ km/h}\) (includes PIEV time) = \(174\text{ m}\)
    • 6/6 vision reading distance = \(48\text{ m}\)
    • Design driver has 6/9 vision
  • Aim: Find the minimum placement distance (\(x\)) of the sign from Zone Y.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Visual Acuity (Snellen Fraction): A person with 6/9 vision needs to be at \(6\text{ m}\) to read what a normal 6/6 person reads at \(9\text{ m}\).
  • Visual Acuity Ratio \(= \dfrac{6/9}{6/6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\)
  • Reading distance for 6/9 driver: \(D_{6/9} = D_{6/6} \times \dfrac{2}{3}\)
  • The total distance from where the sign is read to Zone Y must be \(\geq\) the required slowing distance.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the reading distance for a 6/9 vision driver.
  2. Set the sum of the reading distance and sign placement distance (\(x\)) equal to the required slowing distance.
  3. Solve for \(x\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Reading Distance for 6/9 driver:
    \[D_{6/9} = 48 \times \frac{2}{3} = 32\text{ m} \]
  2. Equate Distances:
    Total available slowing distance = \(x\) (sign to Zone Y) + \(32\text{ m}\) (sign reading distance)
    \[x + 32 \geq 174 \implies x = 174 - 32 = 142\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 142 m  |  Accepted key range: 141.84 to 142.32

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: A superspeedway in New Delhi has among the highest super-elevation rates of any track on the Indian Grand Prix circuit. The track requires drivers to negotiate turns with a radius of 335 m and 33° banking. Given this information, the coefficient of side friction required in order to allow a vehicle to travel at 320 km/h along the curve is:
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Geometric Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Radius of curve, \(R = 335\) m
    • Banking angle, \(\theta = 33^\circ\)
    • Design velocity, \(V = 320\) km/h
  • Aim: Determine the coefficient of side friction (\(f\)) required.

3. Core Concepts:

Super-elevation Equation: The general equation balancing centrifugal force against the components of weight and lateral friction is:\[e + f = \frac{v^2}{gR} \]where:
\(e = \tan\theta\) (Super-elevation rate or tangent of the banking angle)
\(f\) = Coefficient of lateral/side friction
\(v\) = velocity in m/s
\(g\) = acceleration due to gravity (\(\approx 9.81\) m/s²)
\(R\) = radius in meters

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert the velocity \(V\) from km/h to m/s.
  2. Calculate the super-elevation \(e\) from the given angle \(\theta\).
  3. Substitute the values into the formula to solve for \(f\).

Pitfall Warning: Avoid arbitrarily using the simplified formula \(\dfrac{V^2}{225R}\) which is for design mixed traffic conditions. This is a racing track, so the exact equilibrium formula \(v^2/gR\) applies.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Unit Conversions\[v = 320 \times \frac{5}{18} = 88.889 \text{ m/s} \]\[e = \tan(33^\circ) = 0.6494 \]

Step 2: Calculate specific centrifugal ratio\[\frac{v^2}{gR} = \frac{(88.889)^2}{9.81 \times 335} = \frac{7901.25}{3286.35} = 2.404 \]

Step 3: Solve for side friction\[e + f = 2.404 \]\[f = 2.404 - 0.6494 = 1.755 \]Note: Option (A) is 1.761. If intermediate velocity is rounded to \(89\) m/s, then \(89^2 / (9.81 \times 335) - \tan(33^\circ) = 1.761\). This rounding quirk is a known trait of this specific exam question. The closest analytical answer is definitively Option A.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.761  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q33
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
The following statements are made related to the lengths of turning lanes at signalised intersections:

(i)    1.5 times the average number of vehicles (by vehicle type) that would store in turning lane per cycle during the peak hour
(ii)    2 times the average number of vehicles (by vehicle type) that would store in turning lane per cycle during the peak hour
(iii)    Average number of vehicles (by vehicle type) that would store in the adjacent through lane per cycle during the peak hour
(iv)    Average number of vehicles (by vehicle type) that would store in all lanes per cycle during the peak hour

As per the IRC recommendations, the correct choice for design length of storage lanes is:
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Traffic Engineering

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Four statements defining methodologies for calculating the length of turning (storage) lanes.
  • Aim: Identify the correct IRC recommendation for the design length of storage lanes.

3. Core Concepts:

IRC Guidelines for Signalised Intersections (IRC:93 / IRC SP:41): Storage lanes for turning vehicles must accommodate the maximum queue generated to avoid spilling over and obstructing the adjacent through lane.

  • Provision 1 (Statement i): To account for the random arrival of vehicles (Poisson distribution of traffic), the lane length is determined based on 1.5 to 2.0 times the average number of vehicles storing in the turning lane per cycle during the peak hour.
  • Provision 2 (Statement iii): The queue length in the turning lane should not be less than the queue forming in the adjacent through lane. If the through-lane queue is longer, it will block access to the turning lane, rendering it useless.
  • Design Rule: The length must satisfy both constraints. Therefore, the design length must be the maximum of the two values.

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate the statements against IRC standards:

  • (i) is a valid IRC parameter (1.5 times the turning vehicles). ✓
  • (iii) is the secondary limiting constraint (adjacent through lane queue). ✓
  • The final design length must safely accommodate the worst-case scenario, choosing the maximum value between (i) and (iii).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Maximum of (i and iii)  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: The relation between speed \(u\) (in km/h) and density \(k\) (number of vehicles / km) for a traffic stream on a road is \(u = 70 - 0.7k\). The capacity on this road is _____________ vph (vehicles/hour).
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Speed-density relation: \(u = 70 - 0.7k\)
    where \(u =\) speed (km/h), \(k =\) density (veh/km).
  • Aim: Maximum capacity (\(q_{\max}\)) of the road in vehicles/hour.

3. Core Concepts:

Greenshield's Macroscopic Stream Model: Posits a linear speed-density relationship:\[u = u_f\left(1 - \frac{k}{k_j}\right) \]where \(u_f\) is Free Mean Speed and \(k_j\) is Jam Density.
Maximum capacity: \(q_{\max} = \dfrac{u_f \times k_j}{4}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Extract Parameters\[u = 70 - 0.7k = 70\left(1 - \frac{k}{100}\right) \]

  • Free flow speed: \(u_f = 70\) km/h
  • Jam density: \(k_j = 100\) veh/km

Step 2: Calculate Maximum Capacity\[q_{\max} = \frac{u_f \times k_j}{4} = \frac{70 \times 100}{4} = 1750 \text{ veh/h} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1750 vph  |  Accepted key range: 1750

The theoretical specific gravity of the mix and the effective specific gravity of the aggregates in the mix respectively are:
questions.explanation:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Proportions by weight (\(W_i\)) and specific gravities (\(G_i\)):
    ComponentWeight (%)Specific Gravity
    Coarse aggregate55.02.60
    Fine aggregate35.82.70
    Fines3.72.65
    Bitumen5.51.01
  • Aim: Calculate theoretical specific gravity of mix (\(G_t\)) and effective specific gravity of aggregates (\(G_{se}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Theoretical Maximum Specific Gravity of Mix (\(G_t\)): Weighted harmonic mean of all constituents.\[G_t = \frac{100}{\sum\left(\dfrac{W_i}{G_i}\right)} \]

Effective Specific Gravity of Aggregate (\(G_{se}\)): Back-calculated from mix \(G_t\).\[G_{se} = \frac{100 - W_b}{\dfrac{100}{G_t} - \dfrac{W_b}{G_b}} \]Note: The rounded value of \(G_t\) is used to compute \(G_{se}\) as modeled by the test setter.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Calculate \(G_t\)\[\sum_{\text{agg}}\frac{W_i}{G_i} = \frac{55.0}{2.60} + \frac{35.8}{2.70} + \frac{3.7}{2.65} = 21.1538 + 13.2593 + 1.3962 = 35.8093 \]\[\frac{W_b}{G_b} = \frac{5.5}{1.01} = 5.4455 \]\[G_t = \frac{100}{35.8093 + 5.4455} = \frac{100}{41.2548} \approx 2.42 \]

Step 2: Calculate \(G_{se}\) using rounded \(G_t = 2.42\)\[G_{se} = \frac{94.5}{\dfrac{100}{2.42} - \dfrac{5.5}{1.01}} = \frac{94.5}{41.3223 - 5.4455} = \frac{94.5}{35.8768} \approx 2.63 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(G_t = 2.42\) and \(G_{se} = 2.63\)  |  Correct option: (A)
